content.user_title: Control Native Desktop Apps with AUV
content.value_statement: Native desktop workflows can fail when automation uses stale targets or mistakes input delivery for success. This skill guides AUV observation, targeted actions, and independent verification.
actual_capabilities: Guides discovery of installed AUV commands, plugins, platform support, and permission requirements.
Guides window observation, screenshot capture, OCR text discovery, and operation-specific target selection.
Coordinates explicit field focus, targeted text entry, keyboard actions, and grounded clicks.
Separates command delivery from independently verified application outcomes using results and observation.
Maintains observed remote Device selection and stops when that target becomes unavailable.
Guides task-scoped reuse through installed plugins or small scripts with bounded waits and semantic checks.
limitations: Installing this skill does not install AUV, app plugins, or OS permissions.
Command availability, targeting, and background input support vary by platform and installed version.
Screenshots and command output can contain sensitive data; default evidence recording uses a local .auv/store directory.
Successful commands and dry runs do not prove task completion; unsupported controls require another available tool or a reported blocker.

use_cases.title: Enter Information in a Native App
use_cases.description: Observe the intended window, focus a field, enter approved text, and verify its complete value before submission.
use_cases.target_user: Office staff working with desktop applications

use_cases.title: Check Desktop Workflow Outcomes
use_cases.description: Inspect application state after targeted actions and distinguish delivered input from a verified change.
use_cases.target_user: QA engineers validating native application workflows

use_cases.title: Repeat an Authorized Remote Workflow
use_cases.description: Preserve an observed Device target while turning a demonstrated workflow into a bounded, task-scoped operation.
use_cases.target_user: IT operators managing authorized remote desktops

prompt_templates.title: Check AUV Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether AUV is available and identify permissions needed for observing [app]. Do not install software or change permissions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: read-only runtime and permission assessment

prompt_templates.title: Fill and Verify a Field
prompt_templates.prompt: In [app], locate [window] and enter [text] into [field]. Verify the full value without submitting, and stop if the target is ambiguous.

prompt_templates.title: Recover from an Unverified Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [app] after the previous action. Check partial progress and focus before proposing a retry. Do not repeat submission or other irreversible actions.

prompt_templates.title: Reuse a Verified Remote Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: For authorized Device [device], inspect installed plugins for [verified workflow]. Propose task-scoped reuse with explicit targets, bounded waits, and independent checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: remote target preservation and reusable automation

output_examples.input: Show an example completion report for entering a query without submitting it.
output: Illustrative result: The intended application window was identified from fresh observation.
The query field was focused, and its full value was independently checked.

output_examples.input: Show an example report when a selected remote Device becomes unavailable.
output: Illustrative result: The selected remote Device is unavailable, so further actions stopped.
No fallback to the local desktop occurred.
The workflow remains incomplete until the selected Device is accessible.

best_practices: Read installed command help and refresh observations before selecting a window, control, or remote Device.
Verify complete field values and final application state; stop before repeating actions with uncertain effects.
Use authorized targets and a controlled evidence directory; protect stored screenshots and output containing sensitive information.
anti_patterns: Reusing stale coordinates or identifiers after changing tools, windows, display scale, or remote targets.
Treating successful command delivery or a dry run as proof that the user goal was achieved.
Changing permissions, starting listeners, enrolling credentials, or retrying submissions without appropriate authorization.

faq.question: Does installing this skill install AUV?
faq.answer: No. AUV, its plugins, and required OS permissions are separate setup requirements.

faq.question: Does the skill require MCP?
faq.answer: No. The CLI supports local core operations. An already connected MCP server can be used after discovering its actual tool schemas.

faq.question: Which operating systems can it guide?
faq.answer: The references describe macOS, Linux, and Windows support. Individual commands and targeting options vary; installed help determines available behavior.

faq.question: Which permissions may AUV need?
faq.answer: On macOS, operations may require Accessibility, Screen Recording, or Automation permissions. The user grants permissions; the skill forbids automatic changes.

faq.question: Where is desktop evidence stored?
faq.answer: Default recording uses .auv/store under the working directory. A task-local store root can be selected; stored captures may contain sensitive data.

faq.question: How does the skill confirm success?
faq.answer: It checks direct results and independently observes the application outcome. Delivered input alone is not treated as verified completion.
